article_notes: Ukrainian clinic study (Zhytomyr): 20 dogs with acute spontaneous babesiosis (smear diagnosis, species not identified) and 20 healthy controls. The authors compare an early 'anaemic' form with a later 'jaundiced' form, which they describe as more severe (mortality about 40% in the icteric form). These look like successive stages in the same dogs rather than independent severity groups; group sizes per form are not stated, and table asterisks refer to the control comparison. Only the liver-profile paragraph states significance between forms. Treatment and sample timing relative to treatment not stated. Reported as M±m, read as mean ± SEM.

severity_definitions.label: jaundiced (late) form vs anaemic (early) form
severity_definitions.definition: Authors describe acute spontaneous babesiosis as successive forms: anaemic (early, without jaundice) and jaundiced (late, icterus from about day 3, worse condition, reported mortality about 40%). Blood was tested at both stages in the experimental group of 20 dogs; it is not stated whether the two columns are the same dogs at two times or different dogs.
severity_definitions.severe_group: jaundiced form (experimental group n=20; n per form not stated)
severity_definitions.comparison_group: anaemic form (experimental group n=20; n per form not stated)
severity_definitions.quote: Blood tests of dogs with acute spontaneous babesiosis were performed at different stages of the disease, which were defined as anemic (early) and jaundiced (late) forms. It was found that the changes found in sick animals are dynamically deteriorating and in the jaundiced form is more severe than in the anemic.
